description.summary: one Escape press for a transient surface without the keyboard

protocol.description:
A dropdown that leaves the keyboard with the focused window still closes on Escape in every other toolkit's idiom, yet no standard protocol lets a client take one key from the window that holds the keyboard. Taking the whole keyboard brings back the trap the dropdown exists to avoid.
This protocol takes that one key and nothing else: while a client holds an arm, the compositor keeps the next unmodified Escape press from the focused client, and its matching release, and tells the armed client.
The keysym is resolved in the keymap of the keyboard that produced the key, so a key remapped to Escape counts and a key remapped away does not. Escape is unmodified when no modifier is depressed or latched; locked modifiers such as Caps Lock do not count.
The arm takes precedence over the focused client and over nothing else. In this order, the key goes to:
- the compositor's own key bindings, so a client cannot shadow a binding on bare Escape; - the session lock surface, while the session is locked; - a popup grab, a keyboard-interactive exclusive layer surface, an input method's keyboard grab or a drag and drop session, of any client, while one exists; - the focused surface, while it has a keyboard shortcuts inhibitor, which asked for every key including this one; - the armed client's wl_keyboard, while it holds the keyboard focus, as any key: no pressed event is sent, so one press never arrives twice; - the newest arm; - the focused surface.

interface.name: lys_escape_manager_v1
interface.description: A privileged global: compositors hide it from sandboxed clients.

request.name: arm
request.description: Creates an arm that lasts until its pressed event or its destruction. When several clients hold one, only the newest receives the press.

interface.name: lys_escape_arm_v1

description.summary: a claim on one Escape press

interface.description: A one-shot claim: a client that stopped reading its socket costs the user a single key press. The arm dies with the client that holds it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Disarms. A press already taken stays taken: its release is still kept from the focused client, so the client never sees half a key.

event.name: pressed
event.description: Escape went down and the focused client did not see it, and will not see its release or any repeat. The arm is spent and takes no further press; the client destroys it.
